author: Ahmed Ibrahim
title: Equine America: Europe & France Success Story
text:
Equine America: From US Imports to 70% French Manufacturing and Global Leadership in Horse Supplements Equine America has rapidly ascended to become a leading provider of equine nutritional supplements, strategically shifting its production base to France to better serve the European market.
Founded on the principle of bringing innovative American equine nutrition to Europe, Equine America has undergone a significant transformation since its inception in the 1980s. The company initially focused on importing cutting-edge products from the United States, a market then far ahead in equine nutritional science.
“In the 1980s, the United States was far ahead of Europe and the rest of the world in terms of equine nutrition,” explains Lee Middleton, manager of Equine America, following the transition from her parents, Phil and Julie Middleton, and Bruce Snipes. “My father was then friends with Bruce Snipes, who marketed Red Cell and Ice Tight made in South Carolina.” This early collaboration laid the foundation for a brand built on quality and efficacy.
By 1997, Equine America had established itself as a distinct brand, notably with the launch of Cortaflex, the first widely marketed joint supplement for horses. “Bruce and my father were very invested and always looking for the right product,” Middleton recalls. “At the end of the 1990s, they put Cortaflex on the market, an alternative supplement to glucosamine products, intended to provide joint support. It is still our bestseller to this day, with more than three million sales divided between him and his variants!”
In 2018, Middleton acquired the brand and initiated a shift in production, beginning in the United Kingdom to end twenty-five years of imports. The 2020 Brexit vote further accelerated this strategy. “Brexit was a complicated trade situation, so we finally decided to open a European subsidiary, especially in France and Germany,” Middleton states. “These new locations have allowed us to invest in the European market more broadly.”
Today, approximately 70% of Equine America’s products for the European market are manufactured at its facility near Paris. This strategic move has solidified the company’s position as a market leader. The company also maintains subsidiaries in Helmond, the Netherlands, and Sotogrande, Spain, expanding its reach across the continent.
Equine America’s success is also fueled by strong partnerships with prominent European horsemen, including Harrie Smolders, Willem Greve, Yuri Mansur, Boyd Exell, and, most recently, Roger-Yves Bost. “We have many European ambassadors horsemen…and, recently, we can count on the support of Bosty, which is an excellent link with France,” Middleton notes. The brand also sponsors numerous horses competing at the CSI5* level across Europe, demonstrating a commitment to supporting equine well-being and performance.
The company’s team of equine veterinarians and nutritionists are dedicated to formulating products using the best natural ingredients, while adhering to the stringent anti-doping rules of the International Equestrian Federation (FEI). Ongoing research and development are central to Equine America’s strategy, leading to innovations like Cortaflex Super Fenn, Cortaflex HA, and Cortaflex Recovery, which incorporates natural anti-inflammatory ingredients such as boswellia, grape seed extract, and vitamin E.
Recognizing the growing importance of gut health, Equine America has also introduced products like Fast Fix Opti-biome and ULS-GARD, which contain pre-, pro-, and post-biotics. “Understanding the intestinal flora is a burning subject right now,” Middleton emphasizes. “Our most recent products…provide pre-, pro and post-biotic pre-posts!”
Equine America’s expansion extends beyond Europe, with a strong presence in the Middle East, New Zealand, and recent additions including the United States, Chile, Venezuela, and South Africa. “This enlargement of our horizons does not make us lose sight of our quality race,” Middleton assures. The company continues to collaborate with leading veterinary universities to refine its product range and advance equine health.
Equine america: Beyond Joint Supplements – A Holistic Approach to Equine Health Building on its success with joint health, Equine america has expanded its focus to encompass a more holistic approach to equine health. The company recognized that joint support, while critical, is just one piece of the puzzle.Equine America is actively developing products targeting gut health, respiratory function, and overall well-being . This comprehensive strategy strengthens its leadership in the competitive equine supplement market.
The increasing understanding of the equine microbiome has driven much of this expansion. As mentioned, Equine America’s investment in pre-, pro- and post-biotics, such as those found in Fast Fix Opti-biome and ULS-GARD, demonstrates an acknowledgment of the gut’s pivotal role. The company understands that a healthy gut supports all aspects of equine health, from nutrient absorption to immune function. This commitment reflects a desire to go beyond simply treating symptoms to improving overall horse health.
Here’s a closer look at Equine America’s evolving product range:
Joint Support: Continuing its legacy with products like Cortaflex, the brand continues to refine and expand its joint support offerings. Gut Health: A growing focus, with products like Fast Fix Opti-biome and ULS-GARD designed to optimize the intestinal flora. Equine America is committed to providing research-backed gut health solutions. Respiratory Health: Products designed to support respiratory function are likely to enter the catalog,given the common need for such support among performance horses. Overall Wellness Products: Including products like electrolytes, vitamins, and minerals, Equine America aims to provide a complete nutritional profile for the horse. The company’s commitment to research and development is central to this evolution.Partnerships with leading veterinary universities enable Equine America to stay at the forefront of scientific advancements. These collaborations ensure that products are formulated with the best natural ingredients and meet the highest standards of efficacy and safety. This is especially important in the anti-doping landscape of professional horse sports, were the company readily complies with FEI regulations. Equine America is always on the lookout for new, innovative ways to help horses of all disciplines perform at the top of thier game.
Equine America’s international presence, from the European market to the Middle East, and reaching into new markets like the United States and South Africa, reflects its global ambition. A strong distribution network ensures products are readily available. Furthermore, the company’s dedication to its ambassadors and sponsors, especially its support of numerous horses competing at the CSI5* level, solidifies its reputation and supports the broader equestrian community — and, of course, the athletes, both four- and two-legged.
Equine america’s shift toward a holistic approach to equine health, focusing on a broader range of nutritional needs, positions the company as a leader in progressive equine care. By expanding R&D and deepening ties with horsemen, Equine America continues to grow in expertise to serve the changing demands of the market.
Frequently Asked Questions Here are some common questions about Equine America’s approach to equine health:
what is the importance of gut health in horses? A healthy gut is crucial for horses as it impacts nutrient absorption, immune function, and overall well-being.Products like Fast fix opti-biome and ULS-GARD support a balanced gut microbiome.
Does Equine america use natural ingredients in its products? Yes, equine America prioritizes the use of natural ingredients in product formulations while adhering to strict anti-doping rules.
How does equine America ensure the efficacy of its products? Through ongoing research and development, partnerships with veterinary universities, and strong relationships with leading horsemen, Equine America strives to ensure its products are effective and beneficial.
Where is Equine America’s primary manufacturing facility located? approximately 70% of Equine America’s products for the European market are manufactured in a facility located near Paris.
